title: A key written twice in one object
text: `sheriff validate` reads each file it validates as text and counts the keys of each object.
reason: A parser keeps one of the two values and drops the other without a word, so only the text shows a key written twice.

title: The schema and a project's extension
text:
`sheriff validate` validates each file with a JSON Schema validator against the base schema of the SpecSheriff guidelines, composed with the project's extension (§s-eferktypcj7njt5).

The extension is validated first, against the schema of an extension. That schema lets an extension add only kinds, fields of an existing kind, and properties of a file or of a link.

What the extension adds joins the base schema:

- its kinds join the kinds a node may have;
- its conditions join those every node is held to;
- its properties of a file and of a link join those a file and a link may hold.

`sheriff binding` validates each file against the same schema before it checks anything.

`sheriff reindex` validates each file once it has merged each key written twice and changed what an earlier release wrote, as §s-f5rz6b7dhxejjts says, and before it computes anything. It leaves out of that validation only what it writes itself:

- the links pointing at a node;
- outside the archive, a sid a node lacks, every location, a header's index of its sections, the values gathered beside a field and the status of a section and of a domain's header.

Where the schema refuses a file, or the schema of an extension refuses the project's extension, each of the two commands names that file or the extension and every refusal in it. It then checks nothing more, and `sheriff reindex` writes no file.
reason: Each command is written for the shape the schema gives a file. Only a validation against the schema names where a file departs from that shape and what is wrong there. `sheriff reindex` builds each file from all of them, so writing only some would leave the files disagreeing with one another. A key written twice is merged first, since a file read without the merge holds only its last value. What an earlier release wrote is changed first, since the schema refuses its old names. What `sheriff reindex` writes itself is left out, since a node written by hand lacks it until the command runs.

title: Sids, locations, terms and names of RecordTypes, counted
text:
`sheriff validate` collects every sid, location, term and RecordType's name, and counts each.

- A term and a RecordType's name are counted in lower case.
- For each term node, the part it stands in is looked up.

title: Locations computed anew
text: `sheriff validate` computes in memory the location of each node from where it is, and compares it with the location its file holds.

title: An approved node's approval
text:
`sheriff validate` looks up in the approvals each approved node outside the SpecSheriff guidelines the project takes, a section and a domain's header left out. The latest line for the node's sid and the fingerprint of its wording must be an approval.

For each approval the commit adds to the approvals of its parent, read as `sheriff reindex` would rewrite them (§s-f5rz6b7dhxejjts), `sheriff validate` looks up whoever the line names among the owners of its node, as the commit holds them.

title: A removed node and the archive
text:
`sheriff validate` looks up in the approvals each sid a commit removes from the specification.

- A node an approval was ever given for, but a section and a domain's header, is looked up in the archive, with the reason for its removal.
- Any other node is refused where it stands in the archive.

title: Outgoing links and citations
text:
`sheriff validate` resolves the target of every outgoing link among the sids that exist. It reads the citations in every node and sets them against the links the node makes:

- A `§` followed by a sid and then by no lower-case letter or digit cites that sid.
- A `§` followed by anything else, up to a space, a comma, a semicolon or a closing parenthesis, is a citation by a location.
- Text in backticks counts in the check as any other text does, except a citation by a location (§s-bpdqd9v72wg7vsz).
- A header's index and the values gathered beside a field are not read.
reason: A node may show, in backticks, what a refused citation looks like.

title: The kinds at the ends of a link
text: `sheriff validate` looks up the kind of the node at each end of every outgoing link and sets it against the link's type.

title: Indexes, incoming links, gathered values and the statuses of sections and headers, rebuilt
Words running in capitals
text:
`sheriff validate` reads the title, text and reason of every approved node, and of every section and domain's header, for three words or more running in capitals.

- Each such word has two characters or more.
- The words are separated only by spaces or tabs.
- Anything in backticks or double quotation marks is left out.

title: A section with a rule in it
text: `sheriff validate` reads the children of every section, and those of each section inside it, for a node that counts as a rule (§s-7445ahgjck2aefg).

title: Consumes and exempts links
No circular dependency between the domains
text: `sheriff validate` walks the domains along the consumes links, from each domain's header to the domains whose sections it names. Where the walk comes back to a domain it has already passed, the check refuses the change and names the domains along that circle.

title: A used domain's RecordType, only from the declared sections
text:
A using domain takes a RecordType of a used domain only from the sections its domain's header names in its consumes links. Otherwise `sheriff validate` reports it (§s-5yvpn4zhuqmv5bq).

- A RecordType names another by a field's type or by its refines link.
- The report gives the sid of the RecordType that names the other. The change is not refused.

title: A header's level
text: `sheriff validate` looks up the level each header names in the list the project's own guidelines hold.

title: What a RecordType variant must agree with
An identifier followed to its end
text:
`sheriff validate` looks up the RecordType that each field of type identifier of names, and looks up among that RecordType's fields the one it names as identifying it.

- Where that field is itself an identifier, the RecordType it names is followed in the same way, until a field of another type is reached.
- A RecordType reached twice is refused.

title: Where the values of a field of type one of are collected
An object in a list
text: `sheriff validate` reads each member of a rule's list that is an object for the property the list names (§s-v7vd4ydrwexsgsj). A member lacking it is refused.

title: No copy of the SpecSheriff guidelines
Implements and refines links of the appendices and a project's own guidelines
text: `sheriff validate` resolves the outgoing implements and refines links of each node but a section, and reads the part of the node each names.

title: A file of the technical appendix named after a domain
text: `sheriff validate` looks up among the domains the name of each file of the technical appendix but `stack.json` and `debt.json`.

title: How a project's own check is run
text:
`sheriff validate` runs each check a project's own guidelines add (§s-2fau85dfyyeq66m), by the command the settings name for it.

- The check runs in the directory the other checks read.
- The check is handed on its standard input what `sheriff model` prints.
- An exit status other than zero refuses, or is reported where the rule listing the check says it reports.
- What the check printed is shown with it.

title: The symbols a commit changes
text:
`sheriff binding` finds which symbols of the system's code outside its tests the commit changes.

- A changed line counts for the symbol it stands in. A change anywhere in a symbol is a change of the whole symbol.
- A line holding a SpecTag, before the commit or after it, counts for the symbol the SpecTag marks, even where it stands outside the symbol's body.

A symbol does not count as changed where each of its changed lines:

- is not a line holding a SpecTag;
- differs from the line it replaces only in a comment, in the sid a citation names, or in an identifier the commit renames throughout.

title: SpecTags on the system's code
text:
A SpecTag links a symbol to the node the symbol implements. `sheriff binding` reads the SpecTag of every symbol of the system's code. The system's code is the code that implements the specification, its tests included.

- A test carries its SpecTag in its name or in a mark on it (§s-zrsc6asgmhv8tnc), so the symbols of the tests are not read.
- The repository's configuration, its own tools and their tests are not the system's code (§s-hheus6f395ynqvc), and are not read.
- An inner symbol is covered by the SpecTag of the symbol it stands in.
- The sid of a SpecTag is looked up among the nodes, and that of a SpecTag on a changed symbol among the approved ones. A symbol changes where a line the commit changes counts for it (§s-2x58az67bm6cxq2).
- While the commit leaves the specification a draft (§s-j9r8z4xdrfkfs47), a symbol carrying no SpecTag that the commit does not change is reported by the symbol, not refused (§s-kkbqcb9xrpaepwn).

title: From a draft to an approved specification, and back
text:
`sheriff binding` holds the specification's passage from a draft to approved and back (§s-qzthyh7yqvfhsa2). It reads the rule that approves the specification in `project.json`. It takes the specification before a commit as the commit's first parent holds it, read as `sheriff reindex` would rewrite it (§s-f5rz6b7dhxejjts), and as a draft where the commit has no parent.

While the commit leaves the specification a draft, a symbol of the system's code outside its tests that carries no SpecTag is reported rather than refused where the commit does not change it, and so is a test (§s-kkbqcb9xrpaepwn). While the commit leaves it approved, both are refused.

A commit that puts the specification back to draft passes only where it adds to the approvals a withdrawal of that rule's approval, of whichever wording, whose `by` is one of the specification's owners as the commit holds them.

title: The SpecTags the tests carry
text:
`sheriff binding` reads every test for the SpecTag it carries.

- A test's SpecTag is resolved against the rules, the terms and the nodes of a project's own kind. That of a test whose text the commit changes is resolved against the approved ones.
- A test whose only change puts `@spec ` before the bare sid it carried (§s-f5rz6b7dhxejjts) does not count as changed (§s-rah8b37kytb682y).
- A test carrying a bare sid carries no SpecTag. Whatever is reported or refused for it names `sheriff reindex`, which writes the SpecTag.
- While the commit leaves the specification a draft (§s-j9r8z4xdrfkfs47), a test carrying no SpecTag that the commit does not change is reported by the test, not refused (§s-kkbqcb9xrpaepwn).
- The sids of the SpecTags on the changed symbols are looked up among the sids the tests' SpecTags name.
- For each of the project's own checks and generators whose code the commit changes, the sid of the rule listing it is looked up among the sids the tests' SpecTags name. The code of such a check or generator is the files the settings name as its code.
- Each test in the files the settings name as the tests of a project's own check or generator is read for the SpecTag of the rule listing it (§s-sfjka4zc4rhfu67).

title: A node's lists of code and tests
text: `sheriff binding` collects the SpecTags on the code and on the tests across the repository, and compares them with each node's lists of code and tests.

title: A list and its declaration
text: `sheriff binding` compares the members of each list a node holds with the declaration the list names in the code, the schema or the settings. A member that is an object is compared by the property the list names.

title: Citing a node only by its sid
text:
Wherever a node is cited, a rule, a term or a node of a project's own kind, it is cited by its sid, never by its location (§s-kag2m9tzdnduxdx). `sheriff binding` holds every file of the repository to this but those under `specs/`, where `sheriff validate` checks the citations in the nodes (§s-qzyacnqwvaeaps4).

- A location of a node found in a file is refused, in any case of its letters and whether or not the node exists now.
- One exception: the fixtures of the tests of a check that reads citations or locations. Such a test needs a file holding a location, as the data it feeds the check. The files are those the project's own guidelines list as fixtures (§s-6hha5en226aj8hu).

title: Generated copies against the nodes
A node whose tests or code lag behind it
An approved node without code or a test
text:
`sheriff binding` looks up each approved rule, and each approved node of a project's own kind that needs code, among the sids the SpecTags on the system's code and on its tests name.

- A node of a project's own kind needs code unless its extension declares it as needing none (§s-vsh384ybt4w25a2).
- Nodes of the SpecSheriff guidelines, of `project.json` and of `debt.json` are left out.
- A test its framework is told to skip does not count.
- A rule implementing the node through an implements link counts for it, and so, in turn, does each rule implementing such a rule.
- A node lacking a symbol carrying its SpecTag, or a test carrying it, is reported, naming what it lacks, unless an exempts link to it or to a section it stands under exempts it.

title: A citation outside the specification
text:
`sheriff citations` resolves each sid in the code, the tests and the documents against the nodes, the archive's included. It refuses a `§` followed by a number in place of a sid, such as `§5.8`: a node is cited only by its sid.

- One exception: the fixtures of the tests of a check that reads citations or locations are not read. The files are those the project's own guidelines list as fixtures (§s-6hha5en226aj8hu).

title: An edit judged before it is made
text:
`sheriff guard` builds the file as the edit would leave it, without writing it to disk.

- Each changed line counts for the symbol it stands in, and a line holding a SpecTag for the symbol the SpecTag marks (§s-2x58az67bm6cxq2).
- The SpecTags of each changed symbol are looked up among the sids named by the SpecTags of the working tree's tests, the edited file as it would stand included.
- A node the edit leaves approved, a section and a domain's header left out, is looked up in the approvals: the latest line for its sid and the fingerprint of its wording must be an approval (§s-95w92rnjuv3sst8).
- An edit of a file the settings name as the code of a project's own check or generator is refused where no test of the working tree carries the SpecTag of the rule listing it (§s-sfjka4zc4rhfu67).
- An edit of `specs/_approvals.jsonl` is refused whatever it changes, since `sheriff approve` records an approval and its withdrawal (§s-v4qus7raqnwzneb).

title: A commit message names the nodes its code implements
The review of a commit
reason:
A SpecTag says which node a symbol is held to. The checks can tell that a SpecTag names a node that exists, not that the symbol does what that node says. Nor can they tell whether a symbol whose SpecTag names no node carries the system's logic. A reader of the code can tell both.

A changed symbol is judged whole, since a change anywhere in it counts as a change of the whole symbol. The whole symbol is then held to the nodes the commit names. Shown only the changed lines, the reviewer would pass the lines beside them that do what no node says.

title: The tests, run before a push
text: The pre-push hook runs the tests by the project's test command. It runs none, and compares nothing, where the push creates or updates a ref and no commit those refs name holds the specification approved (§s-j9r8z4xdrfkfs47). It then says that the specification is a draft and no test ran.
reason: The working tree is compared with what the push sends only because the tests run in the working tree (§s-477gtdrkw34dzxw), so where no test runs the comparison guards nothing.
